title: Smallpox DNA in ancient Inca mummies shows virus came from Europe | New Scientist
description: The mummies of two people who lived in Chile more than 400 years ago carry DNA from smallpox, providing the first molecular evidence that the virus was brought to the Americas from Europe
author: James Woodford

title: The genome of a long-extinct ancient human is hiding within us | New Scientist
description: We all have bits of DNA from a long-lost “ghost ancestor” inside us – and by putting all the different bits together, we might be able to reconstruct their genome
author: Michael Le Page

title: Woolly mammoths butchered by humans were mostly female | New Scientist
description: Genetic tests of mammoth remains have found a stark contrast in the sex ratio between sites where the animals died naturally and those associated with humans, offering hints about how our ancestors hunted
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Origami-inspired sensor could continuously monitor our vital signs | New Scientist
description: A tiny sensor that unfolds within the body could continuously monitor our heart activity and breathing after showing promise in rats
author: Esra Öz

title: Is district cooling the solution we need for extreme heat in cities? | New Scientist
description: Networks of pipes carrying chilled water have proven to be an efficient way to cool hospitals and universities. Now, they are expanding into cities as heatwaves increase in the US and Europe
author: Alec Luhn

title: Quantum computers are starting to become useful as scientific tools | New Scientist
description: Three problems that are out of reach for conventional computers have been cracked by quantum computers and show how important the machines could become for scientific research
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan
